title: 111. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Percentage Point Change versus Percentage Change
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Percentage Point Change from Two Percentages
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the percentage point change between two percentage values.
questions.question: If an unemployment rate rises from \(5\%\) to \(8\%\), what is the percentage point change?
questions.explanation: The increase is \(8-5=3\) percentage points. The relative percentage increase is \(\frac{8-5}{5}\times 100\%=60\%\); reporting this as \(60\) percentage points confuses two different measures.
questions.hint: Distinguish an absolute difference between rate labels from a change relative to the old rate.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the percentage change when a percentage value increases.
questions.question: An interest rate rises from \(4\%\) to \(6\%\). What is the percentage change?
questions.explanation: The relative change is \(\frac{6-4}{4}\times 100\%=50\%\). The alternative \(2\%\) confuses the numerical difference of \(2\) percentage points with a relative percentage change.
questions.hint: Identify whether the question requests percentage points or a relative percentage.

questions.concept: Distinguishing Percentage Point Change from Percentage Change
questions.learningObjective: Identify the quantity obtained by subtracting one percentage from another without dividing by the original value.
questions.question: Which quantity is found by subtracting one percentage from another without dividing by the original value?
questions.explanation: A percentage point change is the direct difference between two percentage values. A percentage change compares that difference with the original value using division.
questions.hint: Ask whether the description stops at the difference or goes on to compare it with the original value.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the percentage change when a tax rate increases.
questions.question: A tax rate rises from \(15\%\) to \(18\%\). What is the percentage change?
questions.explanation: The relative change is \(\frac{18-15}{15}\times 100\%=20\%\). The alternative \(3\%\) confuses the numerical difference of \(3\) percentage points with a relative percentage change.
questions.hint: Distinguish an absolute difference between rate labels from a change relative to the old rate.

questions.concept: Percentage Point Change from Two Percentages
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the percentage point change when an approval rating increases.
questions.question: An approval rating rises from \(60\%\) to \(66\%\). What is the percentage point change?
questions.explanation: The increase is \(66-60=6\) percentage points. The alternative \(10\) comes from the relative percentage increase \(\frac{6}{60}\times 100\%=10\%\), which is not a percentage-point difference.
questions.hint: Identify whether the question requests percentage points or a relative percentage.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the percentage change when a market share increases.
questions.question: A market share rises from \(20\%\) to \(25\%\). What is the percentage change?
questions.explanation: The relative change is \(\frac{25-20}{20}\times 100\%=25\%\). The alternative \(5\%\) confuses the numerical difference of \(5\) percentage points with a relative percentage change.
questions.hint: Identify whether the question requests percentage points or a relative percentage.

questions.concept: Percentage Point Change from a Decrease
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the percentage point change when a pass rate decreases.
questions.question: A pass rate falls from \(75\%\) to \(60\%\). By how many percentage points does it decrease?
questions.explanation: The decrease is \(75-60=15\) percentage points. Dividing that difference by the original rate gives a relative decrease of \(20\%\), which cannot be relabelled as \(20\) percentage points.
questions.hint: Distinguish an absolute difference between rate labels from a change relative to the old rate.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the percentage change when a pass rate decreases.
questions.question: A pass rate falls from \(80\%\) to \(60\%\). What is the relative percentage decrease?
questions.explanation: Use the original rate as the base: \(\frac{80-60}{80}\times 100\%=25\%\). The alternative \(20\%\) relabels the percentage-point difference as a relative percentage decrease.
questions.hint: Identify whether the question requests percentage points or a relative percentage.

questions.concept: Interpreting Percentage Point Change and Percentage Change Together
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish percentage point change from percentage change in a single comparison.
questions.question: A savings rate rises from \(12\%\) to \(15\%\). Which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The percentage point change is \(3\%\), and the percentage change is \(25\%\).

options.label: B
options.text: The percentage point change is \(3\) percentage points, and the percentage change is \(25\%\).

questions.explanation: The difference between the rate labels is \(15-12=3\) percentage points. The relative percentage increase is \(\frac{15-12}{12}\times 100\%=25\%\). The alternative uses a percent sign for the percentage-point difference, confusing the units of these two measures.
questions.hint: Distinguish an absolute difference between rate labels from a change relative to the old rate.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the percentage change when a percentage value more than doubles.
questions.question: A loan default rate rises from \(2\%\) to \(5\%\). What is the percentage change?
questions.explanation: The relative change is \(\frac{5-2}{2}\times 100\%=150\%\). The alternative \(3\%\) confuses the numerical difference of \(3\) percentage points with a relative percentage change.
questions.hint: Distinguish an absolute difference between rate labels from a change relative to the old rate.
